$comment: Ground truth for the first real evaluation case. See README.md in this directory for provenance and for what each `source` value means. Onsets are quarter-note positions within the measure, as strings, matching Suggestion.target.onset.
name: schmitt-op207-2-ii
work: Jacob Schmitt, Sonatina op. 207 no. 2, movement II

errors.note: The scan puts the notehead on the fifth line. The single sounding error in the file, and the one no musical rule can find: only two notes sound at that onset, G5 to E5 is a third rather than a spike, and the figure never repeats identically.

verified_correct.note: The scan prints a sharp. F#4 rises to G4 in the next beat, which is what a sharp does. Respelling it as Gb4 would be wrong, and an earlier revision of the spelling rule did exactly that.

The scan prints a sharp, in a diminished seventh (A-C-Eb-F#) that resolves to B-flat as though the note were a G-flat. The spelling rule's one standing false positive on this score, kept here so it is measured rather than forgotten.

unscored.note: Twenty-two slot-level differences between the two files, most of them the same pattern: a sustained note that belongs in its own voice was recognised as tied chord members of the voice above. Not scored, because the raw-to-corrected diff cannot separate genuine OMR errors from the editor's re-voicing choices without checking each one against the scan. No detector addresses this class today; writing one is issue #3 in CONTRIBUTING.md.
